title: Why the G.O.P. Nomination Fight Is Now (All But) Over

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在清晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空中走过七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的后面是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联赛里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用一个不同的初始词。

sentences.zh: 而且我很喜欢一锅端食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，持续助您理解世界，过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受nytimes.com slash subscribe上的特别优惠。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the real meaning of Donald Trump's victory last night in the New Hampshire Republican primary.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨唐纳德·特朗普昨晚在新罕布什尔州共和党初选中获胜的真正含义。

sentences.en: I spoke with Time's political correspondent, Jonathan Weissman.
sentences.zh: 我与《时代》杂志政治记者乔纳森·维斯曼进行了交谈。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, January 24th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月24日，星期三。

sentences.en: Jonathan, are you rolling?
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，开始录音了吗？

sentences.en: I'm rolling.
sentences.zh: 在录了。

sentences.en: I'm right here.
sentences.zh: 我在这儿呢。

sentences.en: Okay, very good.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常棒。

sentences.en: So, it is, at this very moment, 11.03 p.m., and we have almost the full results of the New Hampshire primary.
sentences.zh: 所以，就在此时此刻，晚上11点03分，我们几乎拿到了新罕布什尔州初选的全部结果。

sentences.en: I think 70-some percent of the votes are in.
sentences.zh: 我想大概有70%多的选票已经统计出来了。

sentences.en: So just walk us through the top-line numbers.
sentences.zh: 给我们大致介绍一下核心数据吧。

sentences.en: So it looks like Donald Trump has beat Nikki Haley in New Hampshire by about 10.5, 11 percentage points.
sentences.zh: 看起来唐纳德·特朗普在新罕布什尔州以大约10.5到11个百分点的优势击败了妮基·黑利。

sentences.en: That's certainly not the kind of blowout that we saw in Iowa.
sentences.zh: 这当然不像我们在艾奥瓦州看到的那种压倒性大胜。

sentences.en: it's not even as bad as some of the late polling that had her down more like 15, 16 percentage points.
sentences.zh: 甚至也没有某些后期民调显示的那么糟，当时民调显示她落后15、16个百分点左右。

sentences.en: But for Nikki Haley, a loss is a loss.
sentences.zh: 但对妮基·黑利来说，输了就是输了。

sentences.en: She really needed to pull New Hampshire out and it only gets a lot more difficult from here.
sentences.zh: 她本来真的很需要拿下新罕布什尔州，而从这里开始情况只会越来越艰难。

sentences.en: And look what Trump won.
sentences.zh: 看看特朗普赢了哪些人。

sentences.en: He won women.
sentences.zh: 他赢了女性选民。

sentences.en: He won men.
sentences.zh: 他赢了男性选民。

sentences.en: He won Republicans.
sentences.zh: 他赢了共和党人。

sentences.en: He won conservative Republicans.
sentences.zh: 他赢了保守派共和党人。

sentences.en: He pretty much did what he did in Iowa, which was to show that he has control over the Republican electorate.
sentences.zh: 他基本上复制了在艾奥瓦州的表现，这表明他对比对共和党选民具有控制力。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And now I think the question on everyone's mind, let's just cut to the chase, is whether this nomination battle is basically now over.
sentences.zh: 现在我想每个人心里都在想，咱们开门见山地说，这场提名之战是不是基本上已经结束了？

sentences.en: Did Trump just end Nikki Haley's candidacy effectively?
sentences.zh: 特朗普是不是实际上已经终结了妮基·黑利的竞选之路？

sentences.en: Thank you, New Hampshire, for the love, the kindness, the support, and a great night here tonight.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，新罕布什尔州，谢谢你们的爱、善意、支持，以及今晚这个美妙的夜晚。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们。

sentences.en: So after the race was called, Nikki Haley came out to her after party, I'll call it.
sentences.zh: 所以在选举结果出炉后，妮基·黑利来到了她的庆功宴——我姑且这么称呼它。

sentences.en: And she said, now you've all heard the chatter among the political class.
sentences.zh: 她说，现在你们都听到了政治圈里的种种议论。

sentences.en: They're falling all over themselves, saying this race is over.
sentences.zh: 他们争先恐后地宣称这场竞选已经结束了。

sentences.en: Well, I have news for all of them.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我有个消息要告诉他们所有人的。

sentences.en: The New Hampshire primary is the beginning of this process, not the end of this process.
sentences.zh: 新罕布什尔州的初选是这个进程的开始，而不是这个进程的结束。

sentences.en: This race is far from over.
sentences.zh: 这场竞选远未结束。

sentences.en: There are dozens of states left to go.
sentences.zh: 还有几十个州等着投票呢。

sentences.en: And the next one is my sweet state of South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 而下一站就是我可爱的南卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: And she vowed she'll stay in the race.
sentences.zh: 她发誓要留在竞选中。

sentences.en: South Carolina voters don't want a coronation.
sentences.zh: 南卡罗来纳州的选民不想要一场加冕仪式。

sentences.en: They want an election.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一场真正的选举。

sentences.en: And we're going to give them one because we are just getting started.
sentences.zh: 我们要给他们举行一场，因为我们才刚刚开始。

sentences.en: Thank you for the energy.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们带来的活力。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think we have all observed in this primary and in pretty much every primary I've covered, Jonathan, you've covered as well,
sentences.zh: 我想我们在这次初选中，以及在我报道过、你也报道过的几乎每一场初选中都观察到，乔纳森，

sentences.en: that candidates say they are in the race and suddenly they're not in a heartbeat.
sentences.zh: 候选人们嘴上说他们会坚持参选，转眼间说退就退了。

sentences.en: We saw that with Jeb Bush, Marco Rubio in 2016.
sentences.zh: 我们在2016年的杰布·布什和马可·鲁比奥身上看到了这一点。

sentences.en: We saw that with Ron DeSantis just a few days ago.
sentences.zh: 几天前我们在罗恩·德桑蒂斯身上也看到了这一点。

sentences.en: Just a few days ago, remember, DeSantis said he is not going to kneel down and kiss the ring.
sentences.zh: 就在几天前，大家还记得，德桑蒂斯说他绝不会屈膝亲吻戒指。

sentences.en: And then just days later, he knelt down and kissed the ring.
sentences.zh: 然后仅仅几天后，他就屈膝亲吻了戒指。

sentences.en: So, yes, just because a candidate is saying she is going to keep going doesn't necessarily mean she will.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，仅仅因为一个候选人说她会坚持下去，并不一定意味着她真的会这样做。

sentences.en: She has to take stock and decide whether it is good for her.
sentences.zh: 她必须审时度势，决定这对她是否有利。

sentences.en: So I'll ask this question again.
sentences.zh: 所以我再问这个问题。

sentences.en: Is this race effectively over?
sentences.zh: 这场竞选真的算结束了吗？

sentences.en: has Donald Trump, for all intents and purposes, wrapped up, not officially, but in kind of the political realpolitik of this race, the Republican nomination?
sentences.zh: 从所有实际意图来看，唐纳德·特朗普是不是已经锁定了共和党提名——虽然不是官方宣布的，但在现实政治的层面上？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Donald Trump will be the nominee of the Republican Party, barring some miraculous intervention that won't involve Nikki Haley at this point.
sentences.zh: 除非发生某种不涉及妮基·黑利的奇迹般介入，否则唐纳德·特朗普将成为共和党总统候选人。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk, Jonathan, about why this played out the way that it did in New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 那么乔纳森，我们来聊聊为什么新罕布什尔州会以这种方式发展。

sentences.en: Because if you rewind the clock just a few days ago, a political lifetime ago, our understanding was that this was supposed to be a three-person race in New Hampshire,
sentences.zh: 因为如果你把时钟拨回几天前，在政治时间里相当于很久以前，我们原本以为这是一场在新罕布什尔州的三人对决，

sentences.en: a three-person race that would, we predicted, be focused on the battle for number two.
sentences.zh: 我们预测这场三人对决的焦点将是争夺第二名。

sentences.en: That's where we left our listeners off a week ago when we talked to Shane Goldmacher with the sense that unless either Haley or Ron DeSantis dropped out,
sentences.zh: 一周前我们和沙恩·戈尔德马赫交谈时，把听众留在了这样一种语境中：除非黑利或罗恩·德桑蒂斯中有人退选，

sentences.en: they would just muck up each other's path to being competitive with Trump.
sentences.zh: 否则他们只会把彼此与特朗普竞争的道路搞得一团糟。

sentences.en: DeSantis, as we just talked about, drops out in the middle of this past week, a theoretical boon to Nikki Haley, and yet she lost by something like 10 points.
sentences.zh: 正如我们刚才所说，德桑蒂斯在上周中期退出了，这本该是给妮基·黑利的一大助力，然而她还是输了大约10个百分点。

sentences.en: So just untangle that for us.
sentences.zh: 所以请给我们剖析一下这其中的原因。

sentences.en: Well, let's look at Ron DeSantis.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们来看看罗恩·德桑蒂斯。

sentences.en: I mean, by the time DeSantis dropped out, he hardly had any voters, six percentage points.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，到德桑蒂斯退选时，他几乎没什么选民基础了，只有6个百分点。

sentences.en: In New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 在新罕布什尔州。

sentences.en: In New Hampshire, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 在新罕布什尔州，抱歉。

sentences.en: And almost all of DeSantis' voters said that their second choice wasn't Nikki Haley.
sentences.zh: 而且德桑蒂斯几乎所有的选民都表示，他们的第二选择并不是妮基·黑利。

sentences.en: Their second choice was Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们的第二选择是唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: I actually think that DeSantis' departure was kind of a stab in the back to Nikki Haley.
sentences.zh: 我甚至觉得，德桑蒂斯的离开对妮基·黑利来说有点像是背后捅刀子。

sentences.en: DeSantis not only left two days before the election in New Hampshire, but he endorsed
sentences.zh: 德桑蒂斯不仅在新罕布什尔州选举前两天退选，而且他还背书了

sentences.en: Trump and he went out with a blast against the corporatist Nikki Haley.
sentences.zh: 特朗普，并在临走前狠狠地抨击了代表建制派的妮基·黑利。

sentences.en: He didn't want his voters to go to her.
sentences.zh: 他不想让自己的选民转向支持她。

sentences.en: So that was a big blow.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个沉重的打击。

sentences.en: Even though she got the two-person race she wanted, we saw Trump's numbers go up, not down.
sentences.zh: 尽管她如愿以偿地迎来了两人对决的局面，但我们看到的却是特朗普的支持率上升了，而不是下降。

sentences.en: But regardless of what DeSantis' supporters did or didn't have to offer Haley, why then didn't Haley's own strategy end up working at all in New Hampshire
sentences.zh: 但不管德桑蒂斯的支持者对黑利有没有帮助，为什么黑利自己的策略最终在新罕布什尔州完全没有奏效呢？

sentences.en: where she has been on the rise, she campaigned a tremendous amount, And where her campaign said she was a natural fit for this primary electorate.
sentences.zh: 在那里她一直在崛起，进行了大量的竞选活动，而且她的竞选团队说她是这个初选选民阵营的天作之合。

sentences.en: So what made her campaign think that, say that, and why didn't it ultimately bear out?
sentences.zh: 那么是什么让她的竞选团队产生这种想法并这样宣称的，为什么最终结果并非如此呢？

sentences.en: Forty percent, the largest chunk of the electorate in New Hampshire, is unaffiliated, independent, not connected to the Democratic or the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 40%——新罕布什尔州选民中最大的一部分——是无党派人士、独立选民，与民主党或共和党都没有关联。

sentences.en: Forty percent, that is a big chunk.
sentences.zh: 40%，这可是一大块。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the assumption was that most of those 40 percent, the ones that wanted to vote in the Republican primary, were going to go to Nikki Haley.
sentences.zh: 当时的设想是，这40%的人中绝大多数——那些想要在共和党初选里投票的人——都会投给妮基·黑利。

sentences.en: And Nikki Haley had a template.
sentences.zh: 妮基·黑利本有一套现成的模版。

sentences.en: She could have looked back at John McCain's campaign in 2000 to see how you energize these unaffiliated voters,
sentences.zh: 她本可以回顾约翰·麦凯恩在2000年的竞选，看看如何去激发这些无党派选民的活力，

sentences.en: how you get folks that aren't really tied to a political party or an ideology to side with you.
sentences.zh: 如何让那些与政党或意识形态没有真正绑定的人站在你这边。

sentences.en: And that template is to actually reach out to them in a big way to say, I want independent voters.
sentences.zh: 而那个模版就是以大力度主动接触他们，告诉他们：我需要独立选民。

sentences.en: I want a big tent.
sentences.zh: 我想要建立一个广泛的联盟。

sentences.en: You know, voters in New Hampshire, especially independents, really want authenticity.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，新罕布什尔州的选民，尤其是独立选民，非常看重真实性。

sentences.en: They want access.
sentences.zh: 他们想要零距离接触。

sentences.en: McCain in 2000, he would do these town hall meetings that would go on and on and on until everybody had asked every question that they could come up with.
sentences.zh: 麦凯恩在2000年时，会举办一场接一场的市民大会，一直开到每个人都提出了他们能想到的所有问题为止。

sentences.en: There was never a question of him hiding.
sentences.zh: 他从不存在躲避公众的问题。

sentences.en: He was out there.
sentences.zh: 他总是亲临一线。

sentences.en: He was taking risks.
sentences.zh: 他在冒风险。

sentences.en: Nikki Haley, she would go into like a diner.
sentences.zh: 而妮基·黑利，她会走进类似餐馆的地方。

sentences.en: She would give a 15-minute stump speech, and then she would leave.
sentences.zh: 发表一个15分钟的拉票演讲，然后就离开。

sentences.en: Sometimes she would say, oh, I'm going to take questions today, and she would take literally like five questions.
sentences.zh: 有时她会说，哦，我今天要回答问题，结果她实际上只回答了大约五个问题。

sentences.en: If that, that wasn't what New Hampshire wanted to see.
sentences.zh: 如果有的话，这根本不是新罕布什尔州想要看到的。

sentences.en: They wanted access.
sentences.zh: 他们想要的是面对面的接触。

sentences.en: They wanted authenticity, and she just never offered it up.
sentences.zh: 他们想要真实性，而她却从来没有拿出来过。

sentences.en: You know, I was talking to an independent from Dover, New Hampshire a few days ago, and he had told me, you know, I really wanted Chris Christie, but with Christie out of the race,
sentences.zh: 你知道，几天前我跟新罕布什尔州多佛市的一位独立选民聊过，他告诉我，你知道的，我本来很支持克里斯·克里斯蒂，但既然克里斯蒂退出了，

sentences.en: I'll vote for Nikki Haley.
sentences.zh: 我就会投给妮基·黑利。

sentences.en: I don't love her, but I do want to stop Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我虽然不是很喜欢她，但我确实想阻止唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: Well, he reached out to me today and he said, I don't know if you're going to do a follow up story, but I decided I just can't vote for Nikki Haley.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他今天联系了我，并说：我不知道你们还会不会做后续报道，但我决定我实在投不下妮基·黑利了。

sentences.en: I'm going to go and write in Joe Biden's name.
sentences.zh: 我要去写上乔·拜登的名字。

sentences.en: And I said, why?
sentences.zh: 我问：为什么？

sentences.en: And he said, you know, Nikki Haley never asked me for my vote.
sentences.zh: 他说：你知道的，妮基·黑利从未向我索要过选票。

sentences.en: She never gave me a compelling reason for me to vote for her.
sentences.zh: 她从没给我一个不得不投她的充分理由。

sentences.en: And if she's not going to do that, I'm not going to.
sentences.zh: 既然她不打算这么做，我也不会投她。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: So how did Haley's failure in this telling to follow that template and truly persuade independence in New Hampshire to come to her, how did that ultimately manifest in the final
sentences.zh: 那么，按照这种说法，黑利未能遵循那个模版并真正说服新罕布什尔州的独立选民支持她，最终是如何体现在周二晚上的

sentences.en: numbers we saw on Tuesday night?
sentences.zh: 最终得票数中的呢？

sentences.en: Haley won independence, no question.
sentences.zh: 黑利确实赢得了独立选民，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: She won them.
sentences.zh: 她赢了他们。

sentences.en: But she didn't win them by the overwhelming majorities that she needed to.
sentences.zh: 但她并没有以她所需要的那种压倒性多数获胜。

sentences.en: So she also had the other side of the equation.
sentences.zh: 所以她还得面对方程的另一边。

sentences.en: She needed to win a good number of Republicans because ultimately she's running for the Republican nomination.
sentences.zh: 她需要赢得相当一部分共和党人的支持，因为归根结底她在竞选共和党提名。

sentences.en: And she didn't do it.
sentences.zh: 而她并没有做到这一点。

sentences.en: Donald Trump absolutely overwhelmingly crushed her with Republicans, especially with Republicans who identified themselves as conservatives.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普在共和党人中绝对以压倒性优势碾压了她，特别是在那些自视为保守派的共和党人中。

sentences.en: It really showed her fundamental weakness because New Hampshire is not as conservative a Republican base as she's going to be facing in South Carolina and for much of the country,
sentences.zh: 这确实暴露了她根本上的弱点，因为新罕布什尔州的共和党选民基础并不像她在南卡罗来纳州以及全国大部分地区所要面对的

sentences.en: actually.
sentences.zh: 那样保守。

sentences.en: It's a pretty moderate Republican base, but she didn't really win those people either.
sentences.zh: 那里的共和党选民基础相当温和，但她也没能真正赢得这些人的支持。

sentences.en: If you're an identified Republican, you almost certainly voted for Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个有明确身份认同的共和党人，你几乎百分之百投给了唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: And you can't win the Republican nomination without Republican votes.
sentences.zh: 而没有共和党选票，你是赢不了共和党提名的。

sentences.en: And just put a number around that.
sentences.zh: 我们用数字来具象化一下。

sentences.en: How much did Trump essentially crush her among Republicans here?
sentences.zh: 在这里，特朗普在共和党人中到底以多大优势碾压了她？

sentences.en: The numbers are overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 数字是压倒性的。

sentences.en: Trump won about three quarters.
sentences.zh: 特朗普赢得了大约四分之三的选票。

sentences.en: Three out of four Republicans who went to vote voted for Donald J.
sentences.zh: 每四个去投票的共和党人中就有三个把票投给了唐纳德·J·

sentences.en: Trump.
sentences.zh: 特朗普。

sentences.en: Which is really interesting because what that would seem to tell us was that Nikki Haley's 44% or so second-place finish in New Hampshire is kind of misleading because so much of it is,
sentences.zh: 这真的很有意思，因为这似乎告诉我们，妮基·黑利在新罕布什尔州大约44%的第二名成绩其实有点具有欺骗性，因为其中很大一部分是

sentences.en: as you have gotten at, unique to the scale of independent voters in that state.
sentences.zh: 如你所指出的，是由该州独立选民的庞大基数决定的。

sentences.en: And the reality is she did pretty poorly among Republicans who make up the rest of the primary season electorate that she's going to have to contend with in the next few races.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，在其余的初选赛季选民中——也就是她在接下来的几场竞选中必须争取的共和党人里——她其实表现得很糟糕。

sentences.en: And all of that makes a certain sense given that her campaign became increasingly anti-Trump,
sentences.zh: 所有这一切在某种程度上也是合乎逻辑的，因为她的竞选活动越来越具有反特朗普的色彩，

sentences.en: whose main appeal was to the faction of Republicans ready to move on from Donald Trump,
sentences.zh: 其主要吸引力在于那些准备翻过唐纳德·特朗普这一页的共和党派系，

sentences.en: which turned out in a place like New Hampshire to be smaller than the group of Republicans that very much want him to be the nominee.
sentences.zh: 而事实证明，在新罕布什尔州这样地方，这群人比那些极希望他成为候选人的共和党人群体还要小。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: From a message standpoint, she was really in a bind.
sentences.zh: 从竞选讯息的角度来看，她确实陷入了进退两难的境地。

sentences.en: Remember, she first started this as pretty respectful of Trump.
sentences.zh: 记住，她一开始对特朗普的态度还是相当尊重的。

sentences.en: But she said, you know, it's time to turn the page.
sentences.zh: 但她说，你知道的，是时候翻开新的一页了。

sentences.en: It's time for a new generation of leadership.
sentences.zh: 是时候迎接新一代的领导层了。

sentences.en: I'm the new face of the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 我是共和党的新面孔。

sentences.en: Then she started being a little more critical of him on policy and talking about he ran up the debt by $8 trillion.
sentences.zh: 后来她开始在政策上更多地批评他，谈到他让国债增加了8万亿美元。

sentences.en: He's leaving behind our allies in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 他在乌克兰抛弃了我们的盟友。

sentences.en: That didn't work very well either.
sentences.zh: 这招效果也不是很好。

sentences.en: Then she started sharpening her message about Trump personally.
sentences.zh: 接着，她开始把矛头直接对准特朗普本人。

sentences.en: And by the end, she was talking about Donald Trump as an agent of chaos with a brain that seemed to be addling.
sentences.zh: 到最后，她甚至把唐纳德·特朗普形容为“混乱的化身”，脑子似乎开始糊涂了。

sentences.en: I mean, she was getting tougher.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她变得越来越强硬。

sentences.en: And that didn't work either because the harder you go at Trump, the bigger the backlash is against you.
sentences.zh: 但这也没有用，因为你对特朗普攻势越猛，对你的反弹也就越大。

sentences.en: But if you don't go at Trump, people will say, well, why are you even running?
sentences.zh: 但如果你不对特朗普发起进攻，人们就会说，那你还参选干什么？

sentences.en: I'll vote for the original guy.
sentences.zh: 那我不如投给最初的那个人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And if you're an independent, why would I turn to you at all if you're not willing to criticize Trump?
sentences.zh: 而且如果你是个独立选民，如果你连批评特朗普都不敢，我凭什么要支持你？

sentences.en: And so, Jonathan, what we have witnessed, stepping back, over the past two nomination contests, Iowa now New Hampshire,
sentences.zh: 所以，乔纳森，退一步讲，我们从过去两次初选（先是爱荷华州，现在是新罕布什尔州）中见证到的是，

sentences.en: is that you can't beat Trump by running as his political heir, which DeSantis tried, didn't work.
sentences.zh: 你无法通过把自己包装成特朗普的政治继承人来打败他（德桑蒂斯试过了，行不通）。

sentences.en: You can't beat Trump by running as ultimately his nemesis or critic, which Nikki Haley just tried.
sentences.zh: 你也无法通过把自己当作他的死敌或批评者来打败他（尼基·黑利刚刚尝试过）。

sentences.en: You just can't beat him as a Republican, pretty much, period.
sentences.zh: 作为共和党人，你基本上根本无法击败他。

sentences.en: Yes, this is Donald Trump's party.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是唐纳德·特朗普的党派。

sentences.en: And that's why, after tonight, Donald Trump has this Republican nomination wrapped up.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，今晚过后，唐纳德·特朗普已经稳获共和党总统候选人提名。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘（Wynna Liu）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《连线》（Connections）这款游戏，它是《纽约时报》益智游戏之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基（Sam Azersky），我每天负责制作《拼字蜜蜂》（Spelling Bee）和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”（promesthesia）的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的各种游戏都是由刚才你们听到声音的这些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games，今天就开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: So, Jonathan, with the caveat that Nikki Haley does remain in the Republican race for however long she decides to stay in it,
sentences.zh: 所以，乔纳森，在尼基·黑利决定继续参加共和党初选（无论她决定坚持多久）的前提下，

sentences.en: we are now effectively in the very strange position of a general election that basically begins now, 10 months before Election Day.
sentences.zh: 我们现在实际上陷入了一种非常诡异的局面：大选现在就已经拉开帷幕了，而距离选举日还有足足十个月。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, what's really crazy about it is it feels to voters like these are two incumbent presidents.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，最疯狂的是，选民们感觉这就像是两名现任总统在对决。

sentences.en: You have an incumbent president in Joe Biden running against a former president who was only president, you know, less than four years ago in Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 你有一个现任总统乔·拜登，在与一位前总统对决——而这位前总统卸任总统其实也就是不到四年前的事，那就是唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: And people are making a judgment based on, you know, what kind of presidents they were.
sentences.zh: 人们正在根据他们过去当总统时的表现来做出判断。

sentences.en: It feels like an incumbent on incumbent election already.
sentences.zh: 感觉这已经成了一场“现任对现任”的选举。

sentences.en: And we should say this is a general election that improbably pits not just two incumbents, as you're describing,
sentences.zh: 我们还应该指出，这场大选令人难以置信地不仅让如你所描述的两位现任者狭路相逢，

sentences.en: but the exact same two candidates who ran against each other four years ago, one of whom sought to overturn the results of that last election, 2020,
sentences.zh: 而且他们正是四年前相互对决的那两个一模一样的候选人。其中一人曾试图推翻上一次（2020年）大选的结果，

sentences.en: and is now relying on that same system to elevate him to become his party's nominee.
sentences.zh: 而现在却要依靠同一套体制来将自己推选为本党候选人，

sentences.en: knee and then will seek to have that same system elect him president.
sentences.zh: 然后还将依靠这同一套体制选举他为总统。

sentences.en: And that race, that last race where Biden faced Trump and its aftermath was a complete national trauma.
sentences.zh: 而那场竞选——拜登对阵特朗普的上一场竞选及其余波，是一场彻头彻尾的国家创伤。

sentences.en: And yet our political system is recreating that same race.
sentences.zh: 然而我们的政治体制却在重演那场相同的竞选。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And remember, after January 6th, the Republican
sentences.zh: 而且记住，在1月6日之后，共和党

sentences.en: Party had their moment.
sentences.zh: 人迎来了他们的关键时刻。

sentences.en: They could have been done with Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们本可以彻底摆脱唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: At that time, the would-be
sentences.zh: 当时，潜在的

sentences.en: Speaker of the House, Kevin McCarthy, went down to the floor of the House to actually say, no, we are not going to support the impeachment of Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 众议院议长凯文·麦卡锡来到众议院大厅公开表示，不，我们不会支持弹劾唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: Then we had Mitch McConnell going to the well of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 然后我们看到米奇·麦康奈尔走上参议院演讲台。

sentences.en: He had the opportunity to convict Trump in that impeachment.
sentences.zh: 他有机会在那次弹劾中给特朗普定罪。

sentences.en: And after the conviction, the Senate could have easily voted with just a simple majority to bar Trump from ever holding federal office again.
sentences.zh: 而在定罪之后，参议院完全可以仅凭简单多数票投票禁止特朗普未来再次担任联邦公职。

sentences.en: Instead, they acquitted him.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们判他无罪。

sentences.en: So here we are now, and the entire Republican apparatus is coalescing around him.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在走到了这一步，整个共和党机器都在向他靠拢。

sentences.en: They're looking at the Republican electorate and saying, well, if you can't beat him, join him.
sentences.zh: 他们看着共和党选民说，好吧，既然你打不过他，那就加入他。

sentences.en: We saw Tim Scott right behind Trump in his victory speech.
sentences.zh: 我们看到蒂姆·斯科特就站在特朗普发表胜利演讲时的身后。

sentences.en: We saw John Cornyn, who might be the next Senate majority leader from Texas, endorsing Trump.
sentences.zh: 我们看到可能成为下一任参议院多数党领袖、来自得克萨斯州的约翰·科宁对特朗普表示支持。

sentences.en: We saw people like Representative Nancy Mace from South Carolina, who endorses Trump over Nikki Haley.
sentences.zh: 我们看到来自南卡罗来纳州的众议员南希·梅斯等人，她选择支持特朗普而不是尼基·黑利。

sentences.en: And it's not because Nikki Haley has alienated all these people.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为尼基·黑利疏远了所有人。

sentences.en: They don't hate her.
sentences.zh: 他们并不讨厌她。

sentences.en: They just see the handwriting on the wall, and they fear crossing Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们只是看清了墙上的标语，并且害怕与唐纳德·特朗普作对。

sentences.en: They feel like now is the time they have to unite behind the eventual nominee.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得现在是时候团结在最终的提名人身后了。

sentences.en: We should say on the other side of a 2024 ballot and contributing to this rematch we're talking about is a Democratic Party apparatus and leadership that decided that Joe Biden should be the nominee again.
sentences.zh: 我们还应该说，在2024年选票的另一边，促成我们所说的这场复赛的，是决定让乔·拜登再次成为候选人的民主党机器和领导层。

sentences.en: And they worked pretty tirelessly to ensure that there would not be a robust fight over that question.
sentences.zh: 他们不知疲倦地工作，以确保不会围绕这个问题展开激烈的争夺。

sentences.en: And so we now end up with a Democratic nominee that has real questions around his popularity in a general election against Trump,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们最终迎来了一位民主党候选人：他在对阵特朗普的大选中，其受欢迎程度面临着真正的质疑；

sentences.en: who has real questions about his popularity against Biden.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普在对阵拜登时，其受欢迎程度也同样面临真正的质疑。

sentences.en: It is a truism that incumbent presidents are very difficult to defeat.
sentences.zh: 一个不争的事实是，现任总统非常难以击败。

sentences.en: They almost always win re-election.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎总是能赢得连任。

sentences.en: And it was kind of natural for the Democratic Party apparatus, its leadership, to rally around Joe Biden as the incumbent.
sentences.zh: 对于民主党机器和领导层来说，团结在作为现任者的乔·拜登周围可以说是顺理成章的。

sentences.en: But this is a weak incumbent.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个软弱的现任者。

sentences.en: You can look at any polling.
sentences.zh: 你可以看看任何民调。

sentences.en: You can see he's weak with young voters.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到他在年轻选民中支持率薄弱。

sentences.en: He's weak with progressive voters who right now are very angry at the war in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 他在进步派选民中支持率薄弱，这些人目前对加沙战争非常愤怒。

sentences.en: He is weak with black voters.
sentences.zh: 他在黑人选民中支持率薄弱，

sentences.en: who were really stung by inflation and feel like they didn't get all the things that they were promised.
sentences.zh: 这些人深受通货膨胀之苦，觉得自己没有得到所有承诺过的好处。

sentences.en: And he's really weakened among Hispanic voters.
sentences.zh: 他在西班牙裔选民中的支持率也大幅下滑。

sentences.en: He is looking like a weak incumbent, and yet the party powers rallied around him.
sentences.zh: 他看起来像一个软弱的现任者，然而党内权贵却纷纷团结在他周围。

sentences.en: And now we have two candidates running for president that are not particularly popular with the American people.
sentences.zh: 现在我们有了两位竞选总统的候选人，而他们在美国人民当中并不怎么受欢迎。

sentences.en: Despite that, though,
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，

sentences.en: I wonder if there is a way of looking at tonight's results in New Hampshire, just to go back to the main event here, as any kind of a positive development for President Biden.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，我们是否可以把今晚在新罕布什尔州的初选结果——回到我们这里的核心事件——看作对拜登总统的一种利好消息？

sentences.en: If once Nikki Haley does eventually drop out of his race, does it feel correct or at all safe to assume that at least some of her supporters, especially these independent voters,
sentences.zh: 一旦尼基·黑利最终退出竞选，我们是否可以认为，或者说至少有把握认为，她的一部分支持者，特别是这些独立选民，

sentences.en: might be comfortable voting for President Biden in a general election?
sentences.zh: 在大选中可能会放心大胆地投票给拜登总统？

sentences.en: Many of them have told our colleagues that they couldn't stomach voting for Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人曾对我们的同事说，他们实在无法容忍投票给特朗普。

sentences.en: And this is for all kinds of reasons, right?
sentences.zh: 原因形形色色，对吧？

sentences.en: For January 6th, because of Trump's conduct, because of his criminal liability, and so on.
sentences.zh: 为了1月6日的事件、特朗普的行径、他的刑事责任等等。

sentences.en: And therefore, what Nikki Haley did well in New Hampshire bodes pretty well for Biden in November and pretty poorly for Trump.
sentences.zh: 因此，尼基·黑利在新罕布什尔州的出色表现，对拜登在11月的选情是个好兆头，对特朗普则是大大的不妙。

sentences.en: Is that how we should think about this?
sentences.zh: 我们应该这样看待这个问题吗？

sentences.en: When I look at Nikki Haley's 44% of New Hampshire, I don't think that's great news for Nikki Haley.
sentences.zh: 当我看到尼基·黑利在新罕布什尔州拿下44%的选票时，我不认为这对尼基·黑利来说是什么好消息。

sentences.en: I think it is really great news for Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对乔·拜登来说是个天大的好消息。

sentences.en: The fact is, Iowa is not a swing state.
sentences.zh: 事实是，爱荷华州不是摇摆州。

sentences.en: New Hampshire is a swing state.
sentences.zh: 新罕布什尔州才是摇摆州。

sentences.en: And I look at those Haley voters and see a lot of potential support for Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 我看着那些黑利的支持者，看到了乔·拜登的巨大潜在支持力量。

sentences.en: I mean, the fact is, we talked to a whole lot of independent voters in New Hampshire who said they're going to vote for Nikki Haley because they wanted to stop Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事实是，我们在新罕布什尔州采访了大量的独立选民，他们说他们要投尼基·黑利的票，是因为他们想阻止唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: But they fully acknowledged they plan to vote for Joe Biden in the fall.
sentences.zh: 但他们完全承认，他们计划在秋季大选中投票给乔·拜登。

sentences.en: I think that what we see in those Haley voters in the exit polling is a real fear of another Trump term.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我们在出口民调中从这些黑利支持者身上看到的是对特朗普再次执政的真正恐惧。

sentences.en: And that fear is going to show up in a movement toward Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 这种恐惧将转化为向乔·拜登靠拢的政治力量。

sentences.en: That being said, we don't know what all these Haley voters are going to do in November.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我们并不知道所有这些黑利的支持者在11月会怎么做。

sentences.en: Some of them might fall in line with Donald Trump just the way so many other people do.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人可能会像其他许多人一样，最终选择服从党纪支持唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: Some might just not go out and vote at all in November because they don't like their choices.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人可能因为不喜欢候选人而在11月干脆不出门投票。

sentences.en: And they don't have to make one of the choices.
sentences.zh: 他们并非必须在这些选项中做出选择。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And to that point on this night where we feel like we can say that this Republican nomination contest is basically over and that the general election has commenced,
sentences.zh: 说到这一点，在这个我们觉得可以宣告共和党初选基本结束、大选已经正式拉开帷幕的夜晚，

sentences.en: the reality is that polling right now, national polling, swing state polling, shows this to be an excruciatingly close general election race.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，目前的民调——无论是全国民调还是摇摆州民调——都显示这是一场极其胶着的大选之争。

sentences.en: Yes, it's 10 months out, but the closeness of it is kind of extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 是的，距离大选还有10个月，但竞争如此激烈实在有些非同寻常。

sentences.en: And those same polls tell us, each and every one, that voters, especially those who may end up being decisive in this election, are just not happy with their choices.
sentences.zh: 而且同样的每一份民调都告诉我们，选民们——尤其是那些最终可能在这场选举中起决定性作用的选民——对他们的选择感到极其不满。

sentences.en: Most Americans did not want a rematch between Donald Trump and Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数美国人不希望看到唐纳德·特朗普和乔·拜登再次对决。

sentences.en: And that's leading to this real sense of dread, a fear of what is going to be coming over the next nine, 10 months.
sentences.zh: 这就导致了一种真正的恐惧感，担心未来九到十个月将会发生什么。

sentences.en: And even a denial, you hear it all the time, Republicans saying, oh, Joe Biden isn't really going to be the nominee.
sentences.zh: 甚至还伴随着一种逃避心理，你经常能听到这种说法：共和党人说，哦，乔·拜登其实不会成为候选人。

sentences.en: Somehow there's some magical thing that he's going to pull that the Democrats are going to put up someone else.
sentences.zh: 总觉得会有什么神奇的事情发生，民主党会推出其他人。

sentences.en: Or you talk to Democrats and they say, oh, there's no way.
sentences.zh: 或者你跟民主党人交谈，他们会说，哦，绝不可能。

sentences.en: Donald Trump's not really going to be the nominee.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普实际上不会成为候选人。

sentences.en: Somehow, maybe he'll be put in prison.
sentences.zh: 说不定，他会被送进监狱。

sentences.en: It could happen.
sentences.zh: 这完全有可能发生。

sentences.en: Maybe he'll be knocked off the ballot by a constitutional intervention.
sentences.zh: 也许他会通过宪法干预而被取消选票资格。

sentences.en: But the fact is, underneath it all, everybody is really afraid about what is brewing for this coming election.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，在这表面之下，每个人都对即将到来的这场选举感到真正的恐惧。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What you're really saying is that there's some wishful thinking happening right now on the
sentences.zh: 你真正想说的是，目前双方阵营

sentences.en: part of both parties, and it's born out of this sense of denial that you are diagnosing in the electorate.
sentences.zh: 都存在一些一厢情愿的想法，而这正是你所诊断出的选民普遍存在的逃避心理的产物。

sentences.en: I mean, people are so determined to avoid this in their heads and in their worlds that they're basically engaging in fantastical thinking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们在脑海中和他们的世界里如此坚决地想要逃避这一点，以至于他们基本上是在进行不切实际的幻想。

sentences.en: We don't know what's going to be actually going on in this country by the time we actually vote for the next president.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道等到我们真正投票选出下一任总统时，这个国家到底会发生什么。

sentences.en: But right now, nobody wants this conteSt.
sentences.zh: 但就目前而言，没有人想要这场对决。

sentences.en: And how both of these candidates navigate that dread and perhaps propagate that dread could determine who is victorious on November 2nd.
sentences.zh: 这两位候选人将如何应对这种恐惧，甚至是如何煽动这种恐惧，可能会决定谁能在11月2日取得胜利。

sentences.en: Well, Jonathan, it is now Wednesday morning.
sentences.zh: 好了，乔纳森，现在已经是星期三早上了。

sentences.en: Get some sleep.
sentences.zh: 去睡个好觉吧。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们不胜感激。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: We found, you know, some loose bolts on many of our Max 9s.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，你知道，我们的许多Max 9飞机上有一些松动的螺栓。

sentences.en: Many?
sentences.zh: 很多？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So those are things that are going to be rectified through the inspection process.
sentences.zh: 所以这些问题都将在检查过程中得到纠正。

sentences.en: In an interview on Tuesday with NBC News, the CEO of Alaska Airlines disclosed that the company has found loose bolts on the doors of multiple Boeing MAX 9 jets in its fleet.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加航空公司首席执行官周二在接受全国广播公司新闻网（NBC News）采访时透露，该公司在其机队的多个波音MAX 9喷气式客机舱门上发现了松动的螺栓。

sentences.en: It was a startling revelation from an airline that experienced a blown-out door on a Boeing MAX 9 mid-flight earlier this month.
sentences.zh: 对于一家在犹他州（注：原文未提及犹他，依上下文省略地名）本月早些时候在飞行途中经历过波音MAX 9舱门爆裂的航空公司来说，这是一个令人震惊的披露。

sentences.en: In the interview, Alaska's CEO Ben Minicucci publicly rebuked Boeing for the problem.
sentences.zh: 在采访中，阿拉斯加航空公司的首席执行官本·米尼库奇（Ben Minicucci）公开谴责了波音公司存在的这一问题。

sentences.en: It makes me angry.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到愤怒。

sentences.en: Boeing is better than this, and Flight 282 should never have happened.
sentences.zh: 波音的水平本该更好，282号航班本不该发生这种事。

sentences.en: It should never have happened.
sentences.zh: 这绝不应该发生。

sentences.en: And the film Oppenheimer, the subject of yesterday's Daily, won 13 Oscar nominations on Tuesday, the most by far of any film released last year.
sentences.zh: 电影《奥本海默》——也就是昨天《每日新闻》节目的主题——于周二获得了13项奥斯卡提名，是去年上映的所有影片中获得提名最多的，遥遥领先。

sentences.en: The movie, which tells the story of the race to build the atomic bomb, won nominations for Best Director, Best Actor, and Best Cinematography, among others,
sentences.zh: 这部讲述制造原子弹竞争故事的电影获得了最佳导演、最佳男主角和最佳摄影等多个奖项的提名，

sentences.en: and is now the frontrunner for Best Picture.
sentences.zh: 目前已成为最佳影片的头号热门。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Asla Chaturvedi, Alex Stern, and Michael Simon-Johnson.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由阿斯拉·查图维迪（Asla Chaturvedi）、亚历克斯·斯特恩（Alex Stern）和迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊（Michael Simon-Johnson）制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Rachel Quester and M.J.
sentences.zh: 由蕾切尔·奎斯特（Rachel Quester）和M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn, and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley, and contains original music from Marion Lozano and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩（Davis-Lynn）剪辑，阿莉萨·莫克斯利（Alyssa Moxley）负责混音，并包含马里昂·洛扎诺（Marion Lozano）和丹·鲍威尔（Dan Powell）的原创音乐。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由Wonderly乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格（Jim Brunberg）和本·兰斯福德（Ben Lansford）创作。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗（Michael Barbaro）。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个控制严密的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称为改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我主持的最新一期《大都会》节目中，我是萨拉·科尼格，这里讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《大都会》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
